claim: A 2026 LLM-confidence-calibration paper (MACE) evaluates 15 representative calibration methods across 4 LLM families spanning 7B-72B parameters, establishing a concrete evaluation-breadth precedent for this subarea.
stance_target: single-model, single-baseline calibration papers are below the expected scope in this subarea
scope_conditions: general factual QA, training-free calibration methods, 2026 preprint
quoted_support: Experiments across 15 representative calibration methods and four LLM families (7B–72B) reveal that while accuracy increases with answer cardinality, estimated confidence consistently decreases, causing severe miscalibration for questions with mixed answer counts.

claim: Existing training-free consistency-based confidence calibration methods systematically underestimate confidence on questions with multiple valid correct answers because disagreement among equally-correct sampled responses is mistaken for uncertainty.
scope_conditions: multi-answer factual QA, training-free calibration methods
quoted_support: these methods break down in the presence of multiple valid answers, where disagreement among equally correct responses leads to systematic underestimation of confidence
